mappings.note: POOR FIT on half the question: the pulley must be read off the figure as single fixed (LO-3) and then MA and VR quoted. MA is reachable only through C2.6, and velocity ratio has no code in this frame at all.

Asks for the definition of work done by a CONSTANT force - the first half of LO-1 word for word. Nothing is calculated and no unit is asked, so neither LO-2 nor the unit clause is the discriminator here.

The SI unit of WORK and its one-newton-one-metre definition - the '...and its SI unit' clause of LO-1. Not LO-4, which carries the unit of ENERGY; that distinction separates this from the James Prescott Joule item.

The condition for zero work on a MOVING object is the perpendicular case, decided from the definition (LO-1). Sibling item V53 covers the zero-displacement case; both sit on LO-1 because the frame has no finer split.
Supply an everyday example of negative work - the sign clause of the work definition, LO-1. No magnitude is produced, so LO-2 is not in play.

Zero work from zero displacement when pushing a wall - the displacement clause of LO-1, and the counterpart to V51's perpendicular case. Effort felt by the pusher is a distractor, not an energy-forms question.
Asks the student to STATE the work-energy theorem, which is LO-3 verbatim. Chosen over LO-2 and LO-6 because nothing is applied or computed.

The unit named here is the unit of ENERGY, so LO-4 rather than the work-unit clause of LO-1; LO-5 is added because the second half asks what Joule studied - the mechanical-to-thermal interconversion of energy forms.

Names chemical potential energy as the form stored in fuel and food - the 'name forms of energy' clause of LO-5. No conversion chain is traced, so this sits below the interconversion items but on the same outcome.

The claim to be refuted is about TOTAL mechanical energy decreasing, so the conservation law is the discriminator (C-2.6-LO-1); LO-7 supplies the PE-falls-KE-rises justification. Ordering reflects which idea decides the answer.

Defines power (C-2.6-LO-1) and then contrasts stairs run versus walked 'in terms of work AND power' - the work half rests on work depending only on force and displacement, not time (LO-1). No number is produced, so not C-2.6-LO-2.
States KE and PE at the release point and then traces the transformation through a vertical fall - the free-fall PE-to-KE case of LO-7. Not LO-6: mgh is written symbolically, never evaluated.

Lays out the procedure for a power calculation, so C-2.6-LO-2 leads, with LO-6 for the intermediate mgh energy step the procedure depends on. Not a CG8 inquiry outcome - no hypothesis, variable or instrument is involved, only a formula sequence.

Three distinct demands: what simple machines are (LO-3), how they reduce effort, i.e. mechanical advantage (C2.6), and why the total work is nevertheless unchanged, which is the conservation law (C-2.6-LO-1). Dropping any one would leave part of the item unmapped.

Why a real pendulum stops 'despite the conservation of energy' - the item names the law and asks it be reconciled with dissipation, so C-2.6-LO-1. Unlike the perpetual-machine item, no form of energy is named in the answer, so LO-5 is not added.
Bare definition of power, which lives in C-2.6-LO-1's 'Define power and its unit' clause. C-2.6-LO-2 is reserved for items that actually compute a power.
The watt and its joule-per-second relation - the 'and its unit' half of C-2.6-LO-1, the only place in the frame where the unit of power appears. Deliberately not LO-4, which is the unit of energy.
Same-work-shorter-time reasoning applied to stairs; a one-line version of V92 and honestly the same outcome. Kept to C-2.6-LO-1 alone because, unlike V92, it does not also ask about the work done.
The answer is that machines change the MAGNITUDE or DIRECTION of effort: direction is the LO-3 description of what a machine does, magnitude is mechanical advantage, which only C2.6 names.

POOR FIT. Asks for the MA formula (load/effort) outright. Curriculum 82 defines no outcome for mechanical advantage, so the competency statement is the only legal code that even mentions it; no machine identification is required, so no LO-3.

PARTIAL FIT. LO-3 covers identifying a lever, but the item asks specifically for a CLASS I lever and the position of the fulcrum; lever classes are not in the frame. LO-3 is the nearest and only sensible code.

Explains what a fixed pulley does - redirects effort without multiplying it. That is describing an identified simple machine (LO-3); C2.6 is withheld precisely because the answer is that there is NO force multiplication.

Two demands: describe the structure of an inclined plane (LO-3) and explain the mechanical advantage it provides (C2.6). Contrast with the fixed-pulley item, where no advantage exists and C2.6 is therefore absent.

The correction required is that machines cannot CREATE energy - a direct appeal to the conservation law (C-2.6-LO-1), with LO-3 for the machines themselves. Not a mechanical-advantage item: the misconception is about energy, not force ratios.

Two halves: define work scientifically (LO-1) and give the expression used when force and displacement are aligned (LO-2). The paired V49 item asks only for the definition, which is why it carries LO-1 alone.
